decisive_items: Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL (normal, <0.023 ng/mL)
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
response.rationale: The markedly elevated troponin and dynamic ECG changes are diagnostic of acute myocardial infarction; the coronary anatomy findings are supportive but do not define the acute clinical syndrome as precisely.

rejected.why: Total right coronary artery occlusion is angiographically supported and likely the culprit, but this label is an anatomical/culprit finding rather than the acute clinical diagnosis.
Subtotal LMCA occlusion is a significant coexisting finding, but it does not by itself explain the acute troponin elevation and evolving ischemic ECG pattern.
Coronary artery disease is a broader underlying category that is true but too nonspecific for the acute myocardial infarction presented here.
